title: Cerebral Palsy (CP)
lead: Working with children and families: function, participation and growth.
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Delayed milestones, abnormal tone, toe walking, scissoring, asymmetry, persistent primitive reflexes. Ask the family about birth history, milestones, current function at home and school, seizures, feeding, pain, sleep, equipment, previous treatment (botulinum toxin, surgery), and the child's and family's goals. In paediatrics, the family is part of the team. Goals should reflect what matters in the child's daily life: playing with friends, walking to class, sitting to eat. Use the ICF framework (body function, activity, participation, environment, personal factors).
qa: Is CP a progressive brain disease? No, the brain lesion is non-progressive, but musculoskeletal problems can progress with growth.
Why is GMFCS useful? It describes function, predicts motor development and guides surveillance.
A child loses the ability to walk he previously had. What should you suspect? A progressive condition; refer urgently.
Which intervention for a child with hemiplegia and some hand function? Constraint-induced or bimanual training.
Why is hip surveillance important in GMFCS IV to V? High risk of progressive hip displacement.

redFlags.Finding: New hip pain, reduced abduction, asymmetry
Pain or swelling after minor trauma in a non-walking child
Coughing and choking with meals, chest infections

manualNotes: Passive stretching alone has limited evidence for long-term contracture prevention [Ref – to verify]. Combine with active use, standing, positioning and orthoses.
modalityNotes: Functional electrical stimulation and hydrotherapy may support goals in selected children. Choose based on goals, not habit.
